text: The funeral was well attended. The guest of honor was the only one who did not have to pretend to enjoy it.
alt: The white witch stands beside a closed coffin and a white flower wreath in a candlelit room, looking more at ease than a funeral guest should.

text: People say rest in peace as if the dead were the ones who needed the advice.
alt: The white witch sits on a moonlit tombstone with a teacup, as if she is giving advice to nobody.

text: Optimism expired. I left it in the cupboard with the other things I do not discuss.
alt: The white witch opens a dark cupboard and regards one faded glowing jar with complete boredom.

text: The cat has been dead for years. He still knocks the cup off the shelf. I respect the work ethic.
alt: The white witch watches a pale ghost cat knock teacups off a shelf, and she looks almost proud.

text: Coffee cannot repair a personality. It can keep one standing until the evening, which is the same product the day is selling.
alt: The white witch stands in a dim dawn kitchen, hat slumped, both hands around an enormous chipped mug.

text: The crystal ball showed my future. I asked for a refund. It showed me the policy.
alt: The white witch looks into a crystal ball that holds only a closed door and a storm cloud, and she is not impressed.

text: I fly because walking gives people time to tell me about their week.
alt: The white witch flies on a broom over a village at dusk, looking away from the people waving in the street.

text: The houseplant died of natural causes. I was the natural cause. We are even.
alt: The white witch stands over a wilted houseplant with her wand, a full watering can unused beside her shoe.

text: The spell worked. So did the terms and conditions, which was the ruder of the two.
alt: The white witch holds a glowing parchment that has grown a smile full of teeth. She looks betrayed.

text: Sleep is a rumor started by people whose to-do list does not haunt the room.
alt: The white witch sits awake in bed with her hat still on, while loose parchments flutter around the room and her shoes wait on the floor.

text: The mirror said I looked tired. I turned it to the wall. We both have boundaries now.
alt: The white witch stands satisfied beside a tall mirror that has been turned around, so only the carved wooden back shows.

text: I asked the void for a sign. It sent a calendar notification. We are not speaking.
alt: The white witch stands in a starry void and glares at a floating card that shows only a bell.

text: One of the jars is tea. One of them committed. The labels are for guests who still have plans.
alt: The white witch smiles a little too politely beside a shelf of identical dark jars and an empty teacup.

text: Self-care is the locked door. The curse can wait in the hall like everyone else.
alt: The white witch sips tea beside a locked door while a small purple curse-cloud waits politely at the window.

text: I lit a candle for what I lost. The candle asked to be reassigned.
alt: The white witch regards a candle that has melted into a sulky curve and is clearly finished with the errand.

text: My last familiar quit. He said the benefits were immortality and the hours were me.
alt: The white witch stands on her doorstep, unsurprised, above a tiny suitcase and an empty collar.
